newsitem.title: USA: Moody's cites St. Louis operating surplus.
newsitem.headline: Moody's cites St. Louis operating surplus.

text.p: St. Louis' finances are continuing to improve as the city's audited fiscal 1996 results indicated a general fund surplus of about $5.7 million, Moody's Investors Service reported Friday in its Credit Perspectives publication.
The rating agency also pointed out that unaudited results for the first half of fiscal 1997 show the city's positive financial trend was continuing.
"These positive results reflect a revenue structure that capitalizes on its role as a focal point of the regional economy," Moody's wrote.

The rating agency has confirmed a Baa1 rating on $12 million of city's outstanding general obligation debt and an underlying Baa3 rating on $110 million of leasehold debt that St. Louis sold last year to finance a new justice center.

Moody's said the city's five-year capital plan calls for $163.6 million of mostly pay-as-you-go expenditures, although two additional projects that would require $60 million of borrowing are under consideration.
